title: Krishna Chandra Mishra v. State of U.P. & Anr.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
disposition: Petition allowed; s.135 proceedings quashed after s.152 compounding.
headnote: Section 152(1) of the Electricity Act, 2003 — first offence of theft of electricity compounded by deposit of compounding fee with the department — criminal proceedings under Section 135, including charge-sheet and non-bailable warrants, cannot continue. The department remains at liberty to assess unauthorized use of electricity in a civil proceeding under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Section 482 petition allowed; entire criminal proceedings quashed.
facts: Krishna Chandra Mishra faced a Section 135(1)(a) theft prosecution in Case Crime No. 176/2018 at Police Station Chhapiya, District Gonda. An earlier Section 482 petition (No. 807/2021) was disposed of on 19 February 2021 with liberty to apply for compounding within ten days. He deposited a compounding fee of Rs. 4,000 with the electricity department, yet a non-bailable warrant dated 26 August 2021 issued and Charge Sheet No. 01.2018 dated 22 July 2018 remained pending before the Special Judge, E.C. Act, Gonda. He sought quashing of the criminal proceedings.

reusable_constructions.construction: Compounding of a first electricity-theft offence under Section 152(1) of the Electricity Act, 2003 brings the corresponding Section 135 criminal prosecution to an end.
Compounding of the criminal offence of theft does not preclude the licensee from assessing unauthorized use of electricity in civil proceedings under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

holding_units.topic: compounding of first theft offence bars s.135 prosecution
holding_units.holding: Where the first offence of theft of electricity under Section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 has been compounded by the department under Section 152(1) and the compounding fee deposited, the criminal proceedings under Section 135 cannot continue. Charge-sheet and non-bailable warrants issued in ignorance of that compounding are liable to be quashed. The department remains at liberty to make assessment for unauthorized use of electricity in a civil proceeding strictly in accordance with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

principle_tags.application: First theft offence compounded under s.152(1) by deposit of Rs. 4,000; s.135 prosecution including NBW and charge-sheet quashed.
Criminal s.135 proceedings ended by compounding, but the department was left free to assess unauthorized use in civil proceedings under the Supply Code, 2005.

not_decided.point: Merits or quantum of any civil assessment for unauthorized use under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005
not_decided.note: Department given liberty to assess in civil proceedings; no determination on this petition.

authorities.name: Krishna Chandra Mishra v. State of U.P. and another
